name: The Constant
definition: A quantity, relation, or procedure that survives a specified transformation of the observing conditions, always indexed to a transformation class: K(scale), K(distribution family), K(instrument), K(regime)
motivation: The nine source papers fail in a shared way: a result robust at one grade is quoted at a higher grade
refutation_test: Name the transformation, apply it, re-measure. Scale claims are refuted by a scale sweep; distributional claims by a family sweep; structural claims by regime change or out-of-sample survival
precondition: The transformation class must be stated in advance; a constant with no stated transformation is not admitted

name: Grades of constancy
definition: Grade I survives a change of scale; Grade II survives a change of distribution family; Grade III survives a change of regime, instrument, or population
motivation: Gives a vocabulary for the difference between a robust statement and a fitted number
refutation_test: Quote an alleged Grade III rule, then change the regime and re-measure
precondition: No grade may be asserted above the one tested

name: The Existence-Estimability grid
definition: Two ordered binary questions — does the quantity exist, and can it be estimated — yielding four regimes: Compute, Bound, Replace, Avoid
motivation: Most disagreement about risk is disagreement about which cell a problem occupies, argued as if about numbers
refutation_test: State the defining expression, check convergence, then run two independent estimators and compare; disagreement is evidence for the non-estimable column
precondition: The user must be willing to abandon a quantity; the Replace cell contains no numbers by design

name: Ruin, then Estimability, then Size
definition: A three-stage decision procedure in fixed order: enumerate irreversible exposures; classify existence and estimability; only then apply fraction machinery with a discount
motivation: Sizing before the ruin screen computes a fraction for a problem that may have no tomorrow; sizing before the estimability screen computes from a quantity that may not exist
refutation_test: The ordering predicts that decision quality is more sensitive to stage-1 and stage-2 errors than to stage-3 errors; testable in simulation
precondition: Applies to repeated decisions or decisions carrying an absorbing state; adds cost without benefit for single reversible decisions

name: The discount function
definition: delta = 1 / (1 + kappa * CV(mu_hat)^2), with CV = SE(mu_hat) / mu_hat, so the executed fraction is delta times the estimated log-optimal fraction
motivation: Replaces the unsupported convention of 'half Kelly' with a discount that is a function of how well the parameter is known
refutation_test: Check limiting behaviour: delta tends to 1 as SE tends to 0; check that delta = 0.5 requires CV near 1; test out of sample whether discounted fractions dominate fixed half-Kelly
precondition: Requires a usable estimate of SE(mu_hat), which is unavailable in the Bound and Avoid regimes; hence valid only in the Compute regime

name: The four-column reading protocol
definition: Every result decomposed into claim, tool, vocabulary, and technique, with an explicit transfer-of-trust rule from the first column to the second
motivation: Explains why papers whose claims failed continue to be cited: their tools were retained
refutation_test: Fill the four columns for a paper, then find a later paper that uses the tool while rejecting the claim; if none exists, the tool column is imaginary
precondition: Requires the later literature to be searchable; older or isolated papers may be undecidable

name: The irreversibility ledger
definition: A two-sided account of exposures: reversible at acceptable cost, versus capable of producing an absorbing state. The irreversible side is closed to new entries until empty or bounded
motivation: Reversibility is easier to assess than probability and does not require a forecast
refutation_test: For each entry, test whether an exit exists at an acceptable cost; test whether a stated bound converts the entry to the reversible side
precondition: Requires a realistic exit-cost estimate; people systematically underestimate it for illiquid or socially committed positions

name: The scale-span reporting rule
definition: An exponent may be reported only with its fitted scale span; a span below two orders of magnitude shall not be reported as a property of the object
motivation: Exponents fitted over short spans are indistinguishable from the local slope of almost any smooth curve
refutation_test: Take a known smooth curve, fit a power law over the same short span, and show the fitted exponent
precondition: Requires that the data's scale span be measurable, which excludes series with unknown sampling resolution

name: The failure taxonomy
definition: Three ways a summary statistic can fail: noise (the quantity exists and is estimated badly), undefined (the quantity exists but the question is malformed), non-existent (the defining integral diverges)
motivation: Keeps apart three problems that are commonly run together, because each has a different remedy
refutation_test: Classify a proposed statistic into the three categories and check whether the proposed remedy matches the category
precondition: Assumes the defining expression can be written down; where it cannot, the taxonomy does not apply

name: Grade inflation
definition: Quoting a claim at a higher grade of constancy than the one established, by dropping the scope qualifier
motivation: Five documented instances in the source material show the same pattern: qualifier dropped, scope lost
refutation_test: Find a citation that raises a claim's grade; if the qualifier is absent in the citing text, the instance counts
precondition: Requires that the original claim's grade be determinable from the source

name: Self-application rule
definition: Every device in this book is itself graded, and the grade is stated in the chapter that introduces it
motivation: Devices that escape their own standards are how methodological books drift
refutation_test: Apply the device to itself and publish the verdict
precondition: Requires the device to be stateable as a claim, which excludes purely procedural tools

name: The four irreversibility mechanisms
definition: Physical, contractual, informational and social mechanisms of irreversibility, each with a different remedy
motivation: Framing ruin in probability terms misses the social mechanism, which explains persistence in losing positions
refutation_test: For each exposure, identify which of the four applies; if the social mechanism applies and no pre-committed exit exists, treat the exposure as worse than its accounting value
precondition: Requires that the exposure be identifiable and that the organisation tolerate naming individuals' social costs

name: The five bounding moves
definition: Cap the size; shorten the term; add a second source; buy rather than write the option; pre-commit the exit
motivation: Converts an absorbing-state exposure into a bounded one without any probability estimate
refutation_test: Check whether any of the five is available at acceptable cost; if none is, the exposure stays on the closed side
precondition: Requires an exit-cost estimate and a decision-maker able to act on structure rather than forecasts
